meta_description: Predictive Maintenance & Asset Intelligence from Dataq Software: scope, delivery pattern, platforms and committed outcomes.

blocks.x: Where most programs improvise, predictive maintenance & asset intelligence as we deliver it is sequenced: Fix it before it fails — RUL models wired into planning, spare parts and work orders. The sequence matters more than the stack — both are documented here.

Predictive maintenance pays when it changes the plan: remaining-useful-life models feeding scheduler decisions, spare-parts availability and maintenance-window selection. We build the full loop — governed telemetry from the sensor fabric, failure-mode-driven model design (not generic anomaly detection), RUL and condition models validated against work-order history, and integration into EAM/CMMS (SAP PM/Maximo-class) so predictions become scheduled work with parts reserved, not dashboard decorations.

We start where physics pays: rotating equipment, transformers, compressors, conveyors, fleet drivetrains — failure modes with measurable precursors. Clients see the outcome in planning language: unplanned downtime hours, maintenance cost per unit of output, planner trust (the share of predictions acted upon). False-alarm discipline is a first-class design goal; one crying-wolf quarter kills the program politically.

Programs of Predictive Maintenance & Asset Intelligence run in Manufacturing & Industrial, Energy & Utilities, Logistics & Supply Chain, Retail & Consumer Goods — always against one named number, always with the baseline signed first.
What ships, in the order it ships:

items: Failure-mode modeling
physics-informed RUL/condition models per failure mode, not generic alerts
EAM/CMMS integration
predictions becoming scheduled work orders with parts reserved
False-alarm discipline
precision targets, alarm governance and planner feedback loops
Spare-parts optimization
inventory policy informed by predicted demand
Outcome metrics
unplanned downtime, maintenance cost/unit, planner trust rate
